papers.title: Bridging the Sim-to-Real Gap in Parallel-Link Leg Mechanisms via Simulator-Side Dynamics Normalization
papers.summary: Restores actuator inertia, damping, and residual linkage inertia lost when parallel-link legs are represented by serial-tree simulators. Hardware-informed Simulator-Side System Normalization (S3N) improves motion and force consistency, reducing the phase-averaged, command-normalized locomotion gap from 17.3% to 9.9%.
papers.alt: Original paper Figure 3 showing frequency-domain system identification, simulator-side dynamics normalization, policy training, and deployment on parallel-link hardware

papers.title: Design of a Cascaded Disturbance Observer for Robust Quadruped Body Orientation Control
papers.summary: Combines an inner-loop leg disturbance observer with an outer-loop Body DOB for quadruped orientation control. The outer observer estimates roll and pitch disturbances and maps the compensation into leg radial velocity commands, while the inner observer compensates leg dynamics and friction.
papers.alt: Original paper Figure 1 showing the outer body disturbance observer, motion mapping, and inner leg disturbance observer for quadruped orientation control

papers.title: Whole-Body Phase Synchronization via Period Adaptation for SLIP Driven Quadruped Robot
papers.summary: Coordinates independently controlled SLIP legs through touchdown-triggered period adaptation. Correcting inter-leg phase drift prevents early-touchdown-induced gait collapse and maintains trunk velocity tracking in MuJoCo simulations under constant and changing speed commands.

papers.title: Dynamic Friction-Aware Lagrangian Network for Accurate GRF Estimation in Legged Robot
papers.summary: A physics-informed dynamics network combines Lagrangian mechanics with temporal friction modeling to estimate ground reaction forces without dedicated force sensors. MuJoCo experiments on a quadruped leg evaluate joint torque and GRF estimation.
papers.alt: Original paper Figure 5 showing M-Net inverse dynamics and a force observer estimating external ground reaction force

papers.title: Dynamic Modeling of Wheel-Soil Lateral Interaction with Scalable Bulldozing Effects for Planetary Rover
papers.summary: A closed-form lateral wheel-soil model combines transient dynamics with scalable bulldozing resistance for rover motion on soft terrain. Full-rover simulations evaluate its response to changing steering amplitudes and frequencies.
papers.alt: Original paper Figure 3 illustrating soft-soil stresses, wheel geometry, and lateral bulldozing forces in the wheel-soil interaction model

papers.title: Robust State Estimation of Quadruped Robots via Force Observer-Based IMU Bias Compensation
papers.summary: A force observer estimates body acceleration from ground reaction forces and compares it with IMU measurements to compensate accelerometer bias in a Kalman filter. Simulations evaluate reduced position drift and velocity estimation error without exteroceptive sensing.
papers.alt: Original paper Figure 1 comparing IMU acceleration with force observer acceleration to compensate bias and improve quadruped state estimation

papers.title: Mysteric-Net: MIMO Hysteretic Friction-aware Lagrangian-based Network for Legged Robot
papers.summary: Combines a Lagrangian dynamics model with a Temporal Convolutional Network to capture history-dependent friction and coupling between joints. Robotic-leg experiments evaluate inverse dynamics estimation and feedforward tracking control.
papers.alt: Original paper Figure 3 showing the H-Net temporal friction model and L-Net Lagrangian dynamics architecture for robotic leg control

papers.title: TEWD-DFO: A Soft-Soil-Aware Driving Force Observer Using Terramechanics-Enhanced Wheel Dynamics for Planetary Rover
papers.summary: A terramechanics-enhanced wheel model accounts for soil resistance to estimate rover driving forces from internal signals. ProjectChrono simulations on soft soil evaluate reduced estimation offsets without additional external force sensors.

papers.title: SLIP Embodied Robust Quadruped Robot Control
papers.summary: A rotating-workspace force observer and admittance control project Spring-Loaded Inverted Pendulum dynamics onto articulated legs. A Jacobian-based framework connects leg dynamics to trunk feedback control, with simulation comparisons against Virtual Model Control.
papers.alt: Original paper Figure 2 showing the full SLIP embodied quadrupedal control framework

papers.title: A Stable Quadrupedal Jumping Control based on SLIP Dynamics Realization with High Reduction Ratio Actuator
papers.summary: Realizes compliant SLIP dynamics on articulated legs with high reduction ratio actuators using admittance control in the rotating workspace. A trunk-to-leg Jacobian connects body motion to the SLIP-realized legs, enabling stable vertical jumping without passive springs or foot force sensors.
papers.alt: Original paper Figure 12 showing four successive frames of the quadruped robot jumping experiment
